page: Amazon Web Services r8idb.8xlarge is an eighth-generation memory-optimized virtual machine executed on the dedicated AWS Nitro hypervisor platform. The hardware profile is driven by an x86_64 Intel processor architecture with a clock speed reaching up to 3.9 GHz. It allocates 32 vCPUs derived from 16 physical cores via simultaneous multithreading at two threads per core. The compute allocation is dedicated rather than shared, ensuring consistent computational execution across enterprise environments without CPU credit throttling.

Memory and local I/O provisioning constitute the defining capabilities of the r8idb.8xlarge. The server integrates 256 GB of system RAM, establishing an 8 GB memory ratio per vCPU to accommodate sizable resident datasets. In addition to high-capacity volatile memory, the instance features 1,900 GB of integrated local NVMe SSD instance storage. This local storage volume yields high-throughput, low-latency disk operations directly attached to the host, distinguishing it from instances reliant exclusively on network-attached block devices. Network performance is anchored by a baseline bandwidth of 33 Gbps.

Qualitatively, the bundling of 1.9 TB of direct-attached NVMe storage alongside 256 GB of RAM yields strong hardware resource density, eliminating the latency and separate throughput limits associated with external network volumes for temporary state storage. However, local instance store volumes are ephemeral, requiring robust architectural replication to mitigate data loss upon host stop or failure events. Furthermore, the instance contains no discrete GPU accelerators and provisions no complimentary public IPv4 addresses, reflecting a specialized focus on high-capacity memory and local I/O operations.

Given its memory footprint, rapid NVMe instance storage, and 33 Gbps network capability, the r8idb.8xlarge is aligned with data-intensive production environments. Typical deployments include distributed in-memory caches, relational database systems requiring substantial temporary scratch tables, real-time analytics processing, big data ETL pipelines, and search indexing clusters.
description: Amazon Web Services r8idb.8xlarge is a memory-optimized cloud server built on the AWS Nitro System and powered by x86_64 Intel processors. The instance provides 32 dedicated vCPUs across 16 physical cores operating at up to 3.9 GHz, paired with 256 GB of system RAM, maintaining a high 1:8 core-to-memory ratio. Designed for high I/O performance, it includes 1,900 GB of direct-attached local NVMe SSD instance storage alongside a 33 Gbps baseline networking interface. By bundling high-capacity local solid-state storage directly onto a memory-dense hardware footprint, the r8idb.8xlarge delivers qualitative cost and operational efficiencies for environments requiring fast scratch disk access alongside extensive memory buffers, eliminating external block storage latency. With no discrete GPU acceleration, this configuration is technically suited for workloads such as distributed in-memory databases, memory-resident analytics, real-time caching engines, and high-throughput transactional database systems requiring high local disk throughput.
